title: Determinant lines are multiplicative in short exact sequences
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules of constant ranks $r_1,r_2,r_3$ respectively, so $r_2=r_1+r_3$. Define $\det(\mathcal E_i)=\bigwedge^{r_i}\mathcal E_i$, with $\det(0)=\mathcal O_X$. There is a canonical isomorphism of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] $\det(\mathcal E_2)\cong\det(\mathcal E_1)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\det(\mathcal E_3)$, compatible with restriction to open subsets of $X$.

proof.text: Apply exteriorSheaf_top_isInvertible to each of the three finite locally free modules at its specified rank. This proves the three invertibility clauses, including rank zero.

Apply determinant_shortExact_exists to the short exact sequence and the rank relation for the isomorphism with the specified wedge formula. For uniqueness use Iso.ext_inv. Short exactness gives Epi S.g; exteriorSheafTensor_lift_hom_ext reduces equality of the two inverses to tensors of lifted pure wedges. Their given wedge formulas agree on these tensors. This compatibility theorem transports the official exteriorTensor_lift_hom_ext through exteriorSheafPowerIso, so the unit route and the construction of determinant_shortExact_exists are preserved.
